title: Fullness of equivariant torsor restriction at the nodal origin
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $\pi$ a uniformizer and $k=A/(\pi)$ its residue field. Assume the canonical map $A\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/(\pi^n)$ is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. An $A$-group scheme means a group object in schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$: the multiplication, unit and inverse diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with this base in place of the field base. Write $\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finite-type $A$-group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A[s,t]/(st-\pi)$, with $\mathbf G_{m,A}$ acting by $z\cdot(s,t)=(zs,z^{-1}t)$, and let $o=V(s,t)=\operatorname{Spec}k$. A right $H$-torsor over an $A$-scheme $Y$ means a represented right torsor in [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors], with base $\operatorname{Spec}A$. A $\mathbf G_m$-equivariant such torsor has a left $\mathbf G_{m,A}$-action covering the specified action on $Y$ and commuting with the right $H$-action; isomorphisms respect both actions and the projection to $Y$. For any two $\mathbf G_{m,A}$-equivariant right $H$-torsors $P,Q$ over $X$ and any $\mathbf G_{m,k}$-equivariant right $H_k$-torsor isomorphism $\alpha_0:P|_o\simeq Q|_o$, there exists an equivariant right $H$-torsor isomorphism $\alpha:P\simeq Q$ over $X$ restricting to $\alpha_0$. Equivalently, restriction from equivariant $H$-torsors on $X$ to equivariant $H_k$-torsors on $o$ is full; uniqueness is not asserted.

source.place: WANTED locally; read author-hosted https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf. Lemma 3.3 and its proof, printed p.4, expressed as equivariant torsors on the nodal scheme; Section 2, Claim 3, printed p.3, gives the degreewise algebraization calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-torsor-isom-affine-smooth] with $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y=X$ and the given $H,P,Q$. We obtain an affine scheme $I=\operatorname{Spec}C$, smooth over $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R=A[s,t]/(st-\pi)$. Its sections are exactly the right-torsor isomorphisms, after every base change. The two commuting actions give an action on $I$: on test schemes, $z\cdot\beta=a_Q(z)\circ\beta\circ a_P(z)^{-1}$, now over $z\cdot x$. This is natural and therefore defines a scheme action by the stated representing bijection. The action law follows by composing these formulas. A section is equivariant precisely when the corresponding torsor isomorphism is equivariant. Thus $\alpha_0$ supplies an equivariant map $X_1=\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak m)\to I$, where $\mathfrak m=(s,t)$ and $R/\mathfrak m=k$.

source.place: Isom reduction; groupoids.tex Tag 049C; paper Section 2 Claim 3, first paragraph of printed p.3.

proof.text: Here is the coordinate meaning of equivariance used below. For an affine $A$-scheme with $\mathbf G_{m,A}$-action, write its coaction as $\rho(c)=\sum_dc_dz^d$, a finite Laurent sum. Coassociativity says $\rho(c_d)=c_dz^d$, by comparing the two Laurent exponents; the unit says $c=\sum_dc_d$. Linear independence of Laurent monomials makes the decomposition unique. Multiplicativity gives $C_dC_e\subset C_{d+e}$ and $1\in C_0$. Conversely these formulas define the coaction, and a ring map commutes with coactions exactly when it preserves degrees. The same applies to $R$, whose $s,t$ have degrees $1,-1$, and its homogeneous quotients. Affine morphisms and products are translated into ring maps and tensor products by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]; a tensor with $A[z,z^{-1}]$ is just a finite Laurent sum with coefficients in the other factor.

source.place: Explicit coaction-coefficient calculation; schemes.tex Tags 01I4, 01JQ; paper Section 2 Claim 3, graded-coordinate paragraph.

proof.text: Put $e_d=s^d$ for $d\geq0$ and $e_d=t^{-d}$ for $d<0$. Replacing every pair $st$ by $\pi$ writes each element of $R$ uniquely as a finite sum $\sum_da_de_d$: uniqueness follows by substituting $t=\pi s^{-1}$ into $\operatorname{Frac}(A)[s,s^{-1}]$, since all powers of $\pi$ are nonzero. Thus $R_d=Ae_d$. For $N\geq1$, the degree-$d$ part of $\mathfrak m^N$ is $\pi^{q(N,d)}Ae_d$, where $q(N,d)=\max(0,\lceil(N-|d|)/2\rceil)$. Indeed a reduced monomial $\pi^je_d$ has original length $2j+|d|$; the monomials of length at least $N$ generate $\mathfrak m^N$, and in each degree their coefficient ideals are generated by the smallest such power of $\pi$. Consequently $(R/\mathfrak m^N)_d=(A/\pi^{q(N,d)})e_d$. For each fixed $d$, the exponents $q(N,d)$ increase to infinity and attain every nonnegative integer. A compatible family in these quotients therefore determines exactly a compatible family modulo all positive powers of $\pi$, and conversely. The assumed completeness and separatedness of $A$ give $R_d\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_N(R/\mathfrak m^N)_d$ for every $d$.

source.place: Agent monomial computation expanding Section 2 Claim 3, printed p.3; completeness is exactly the hypothesis of the item.

proof.text: We spell out the equivariant square-zero lifting argument. Suppose $D'\twoheadrightarrow D$ is a graded $R$-algebra surjection with homogeneous kernel $J$, $J^2=0$, and $f_0:C\to D$ is a graded $R$-algebra map. Smoothness of $I\to X$, in the affine lifting definition [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], supplies an ungraded lift $f:C\to D'$. For homogeneous $c\in C_d$, define $g(c)$ as the degree-$d$ component of $f(c)$, extending additively over the finite homogeneous decomposition. Write $f(c)=g(c)+\epsilon_c$. All off-degree components lie in $J$, since $f_0$ preserves degrees. For $c\in C_d$, $b\in C_e$, the degree-$d+e$ component of $f(c)f(b)$ is $g(c)g(b)$: each term containing exactly one off-degree component has the wrong degree, and $\epsilon_c\epsilon_b=0$. Hence $g(cb)=g(c)g(b)$. Also $g(1)=1$ and $g(r)=r$ for homogeneous $r\in R$ because $f$ is an $R$-algebra map. Additivity and these homogeneous identities show that $g$ is a graded $R$-algebra lift of $f_0$.

source.place: more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H0 (definition-formally-smooth); elementary homogeneous correction of a smooth lift, expanding the linear-reductivity sentence in Section 2 Claim 3.

proof.text: Set $D_N=R/\mathfrak m^N$ for $N\geq1$. The given isomorphism supplies a graded $R$-algebra map $f_1:C\to D_1$. For each $N\geq1$, $D_{N+1}\twoheadrightarrow D_N$ is graded and its kernel $\mathfrak m^N/\mathfrak m^{N+1}$ has square zero because $2N\geq N+1$. Apply Step 4 successively, choosing $f_{N+1}$ lifting $f_N$. This yields compatible graded maps $f_N:C\to D_N$ for all $N$, starting with the specified map, without any triviality assumption on $P|_o$ or $Q|_o$.

source.place: Induction through successive first order thickenings; paper Lemma 3.3, printed p.4, and Section 2 Claim 3.

proof.text: For each homogeneous $c\in C_d$, Step 3 gives a unique $\phi_d(c)\in R_d$ with residues $f_N(c)$ for all $N$. Define $\phi(\sum_dc_d)=\sum_d\phi_d(c_d)$; this is a finite sum for every element of $C$. Additivity, $\phi(1)=1$, $\phi(r)=r$ for $r\in R$, and $\phi(cb)=\phi(c)\phi(b)$ follow by reducing each homogeneous identity modulo every $\mathfrak m^N$ and using the injectivity in Step 3 in the relevant degree. Thus $\phi:C\to R$ is a graded $R$-algebra map lifting every $f_N$. By Step 2 it gives an equivariant section $X\to I$. By Step 1 this section is an equivariant right $H$-torsor isomorphism $P\simeq Q$; its restriction to $o=X_1$ is the prescribed $\alpha_0$. Only the algebraization of the chosen compatible family is unique; the successive lifts were choices, so we assert fullness alone.
